doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: First Visit in Japan, Abbey Lincoln, Spirit in the Sky and Drum Ode dates
summary: They run through his first Japan record date, the Abbey Lincoln session, Open Sky overdubs, Drum Ode's date, a Bob Moses big-band record, and trumpeter Mike Lawrence.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Or not. I’m going to skip over the live dates, and we’ve talked about Live at the Lighthouse. You did a record with Abbey Lincoln for Japan.

Yes, first time in Japan. Landed with Miles. Like it was in those days, you got off the plane, and you had a record date. It’s unbelievable. I did my first record as leader there, first visit. Stan Getz was there, and who was in the band? Richie, Dave, and Jack. So that’s how First Visit came about. At the same time, the guy said, we’re going to record Abbey Lincoln with Japanese cats and Al Foster. That’s how that happened. That was great. Africa is a great track. It’s well known, that track from there.
Let me just pick one more, and then we have to change tapes for the last time, I would think. We talked about Get Up with It. Then there’s another day with Open Sky called Spirit in the Sky.
Studio?
Yeah.
Overdubs, singing. Steve Satten’s on that.
Yeah. Yes he is.
And his wife.
We talked about Dark Magus. We’ve talked about Drum Ode.
Drum Ode – when is Drum Ode recorded?
Drum Ode was recorded in May of ’74.
Right, because Lookout Farm is ’73. May ’74, just when I left Miles, exactly.
Let’s do one more and then change. There’s a Moses date called Bittersweet in the Ozone.
One of his big-band things.
Yes.
Yeah, Moses, creative Moses, somehow organizing big-band stuff. Not the typical big band, but . . .
With one of the great unsung trumpet players, Mike Lawrence, who died young. I did a few gigs with him.
That’s right. Great cat, man.
Died young of cancer in the early ’80s.
Joe Henderson, The Kicker, right?
Yes, that was his – that and . . .
He was very young with The Kicker, right?
Yes. The Kicker and then the other record he did with Joe, with Herbie Hancock.
I don’t know that.
He’s on a couple tunes with . . .
Is that Pursuit of Blackness?
No. If You’re Not Part . . .
. . . part of the problem, part of the solution?
